abstract: Gauge theory contains an explicit version of the projection architecture developed in Modal Triplet Theory. The full field space contains redundant representatives related by a gauge group, while the physical configuration space is their quotient. A gauge condition is therefore a local representative section of the quotient map rather than a physical law imposed on the quotient itself. This paper interprets gauge fixing as admissible section selection. The gauge-fixing delta is the singular zero-width limit of a representative-selection kernel, the Faddeev-Popov determinant is the Jacobian from gauge-orbit coordinates to slice coordinates, ghost fields encode quotient-measure bookkeeping, BRST cohomology implements admissible quotienting algebraically, and Gribov ambiguity obstructs a global admissible section. We prove a finite-dimensional local-slice formula, state the regularized functional identity under the usual formal path-integral assumptions, and give a typed MTT interpretation. The section language is exact, but the assignment of lens, circle, and nil roles is an encoding dictionary rather than a derivation of gauge theory. A gauge section chooses a representative of an orbit; it neither globally inverts the quotient nor recovers a unique ontic configuration. The global obstruction depends on the topology and orbit stratification of the declared gauge bundle.
